name: Neemo StakingManagerL1 unauthenticated weETH sweep 12 seconds after upgrade
summary: The StakingManagerL1 implementation installed on the UUPS proxy 0x54cd2346 in the previous block added three new external selectors, and one of them, 0x03b79c24(address), transfers the proxy's entire weETH balance to a caller-supplied address with no role or owner check. The previous implementation did not expose that selector, so the upgrade itself introduced an unauthenticated sweep of the staking manager's whole weETH reserve; a searcher called it 12 seconds later from transaction index 0 of the next block and sold the proceeds into the weETH/WETH Uniswap V3 pool.

loss.notes: The proxy's weETH balance was 106.929468097270451433 at the end of block 22855568 and zero at the end of block 22855569; the single anchor transaction moved the whole balance, so the campaign is one transaction and there is nothing left to drain. Valued at the DefiLlama weETH price four minutes before the exploit. The figure is corroborated by realised proceeds: the attacker sold the weETH into the weETH/WETH Uniswap V3 pool 0x202a6012894ae5c288ea824cbc8a9bfb26a49b93 for 114.534059890882021484 WETH, unwrapped it and forwarded the ETH to the sender EOA, which is 287,182.70 USD at the contemporaneous WETH price - 0.04 percent above the marked value, so the sale did not materially move the price and no realised-proceeds adjustment is needed. The legacy 285,700 USD figure was a reported estimate.

ageReset.description: The seventh and last pre-exploit EIP-1967 Upgraded event on the proxy, emitted by the upgrader's upgradeToAndCall(0xbc4b1d58...), selected the defect-bearing implementation one block before the exploit.

sources.note: legacy migration note retained for provenance: onchain review: ERC1967 proxy 0x54Cd23460DF45559Fd5feEaaDA7ba25f89c13525 created 2025-01-13T03:03:35Z by 0xbde590921e7666b0dc88e3b1dd50931c5cd2fb3b, not the attack-tx sender 0xb750e3165de458eae09904cc7fad099632860b0f. Seven EIP-1967 Upgraded events; the last, installing implementation 0xbc4b1d58b28c497b7afda6fb90fe1471fa0672cc, is in block 22855568 at 2025-07-05T21:03:23Z and was sent by admin 0x7e9b11d0aa215e0f1a7f62534c7c93fc340d493d (tx 0xcd4a637da42ef5db0b7b6a1592c99a594530852f91e806d8c12ce0b587579373) - a different party from the attacker. The drain lands in the very next block, so the executing code was 12 seconds old. Reported loss 285.7k USD.

legacy migration note retained for provenance: attacker-event recheck: all 7 Upgraded events precede the exploit tx and none is sent by the attacker 0xb750e3165de458eae09904cc7fad099632860b0f; the final upgrade (block 22855568, 2025-07-05T21:03:23Z) was sent by the recurring operator 0x7e9b11d0aa215e0f1a7f62534c7c93fc340d493d, who had upgraded the proxy 4 times since May. The 12-second age is genuine: the operator installed an implementation exposing an unprotected selector and was drained 12s later

Reviewed the anchor receipt and call trace, every log the proxy has ever emitted, the upgrader's complete transaction list, the runtime bytecode of the old and new implementations, the verified source of the previous implementation, and two mainnet-fork reproductions. The anchor succeeds at 22855569:0: the attacker contract 0x1a61249f6f4f9813c55aa3b02c69438607272ed3 calls the proxy 0x54cd23460df45559fd5feeaada7ba25f89c13525 with 0x03b79c24(0x1a61249f...), the proxy DELEGATECALLs 0xbc4b1d58b28c497b7afda6fb90fe1471fa0672cc, and that frame transfers the proxy's whole 106.929468097270451433 weETH to the caller-supplied address. Reproduced on a fork of block 22855568 from an unrelated EOA with no roles: the same call succeeds and moves the entire balance, proving there is no caller check; the same call on a fork of block 22855567, where implementation 0x9b1f03796ca66240a8a3f159b836c69f951261c9 was installed, reverts, and 0x03b79c24 does not appear in that runtime's selector table. Diffing the two runtimes shows the upgrade added exactly three selectors, 0x03b79c24, 0x53474b2c and 0x97e44edc; the upgrader itself called the other two at blocks 22855612 and 22855836, so these are the operator's own new maintenance entry points, one of which shipped unauthenticated. Victim identity: the proxy answers weETH() with 0xcd5fe23c85820f7b72d0926fc9b05b43e359b7ee and the previous implementation is verified as neemo's StakingManagerL1, so the affected system is neemo's nrETH staking manager, not an unidentified contract. Code history: the proxy was created by top-level CREATE in 0x31ba50b2... at 21612761:100 by 0xbde590921e7666b0dc88e3b1dd50931c5cd2fb3b; scanning all 327 proxy logs finds exactly seven Upgraded events with topic 0xbc7cd75a..., the last at 22855568:130 log 439 selecting 0xbc4b1d58... in topic1; the implementation itself was created at 22855567 by the upgrader 0x7e9b11d0aa215e0f1a7f62534c7c93fc340d493d, whose nonce history shows it deployed and installed every implementation since May and is not the attacker 0xb750e3165de458eae09904cc7fad099632860b0f. Block timestamps 1751749391 / 1751749403 / 1751749415 give a code age of 12 seconds. EIP-1967 slot 0x360894a1... reads 0xbc4b1d58... at block 22855568 and the artifact runtime hashes to 0xb539c286d0d38003ab50ac0c8eee019cf842d42117ee0a9cce6723159fda014d.

limitations: The exploited implementation 0xbc4b1d58b28c497b7afda6fb90fe1471fa0672cc is not verified on Etherscan, so the sweeping function has no published name; it is identified by selector 0x03b79c24(address) and its behaviour was established by fork reproduction and by diffing its selector table against the verified previous implementation.

notes: protocol.slug stays unverified-54cd to match the legacy snapshot row, but this review identified the affected system: the proxy's previous implementation 0x9b1f03796ca66240a8a3f159b836c69f951261c9 is verified as neemo's StakingManagerL1 and the proxy's weETH() getter matches, so protocol.name has been corrected from unverified_0x54Cd2346.
